body:
We currently have the following requirement for 2.5.6.

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **2.5.6** | [GRAMMAR] Verify that forgotten password, and other recovery paths use a secure recovery mechanism, such as time-based OTP (TOTP) or other soft token, mobile push, or another offline recovery mechanism. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 640 |
| **2.5.7** | [GRAMMAR, LEVEL L2 > L1] Verify that if OTP or other multi-factor authentication factors are lost, that evidence of identity proofing is performed at the same level as during enrollment. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 308 |

To be honest, I find it confusing. We want a secure password recovery mechanism but you don't automatically use a TOTP or something for a regular password reset. 

I think I would reword and simplify to:

"_[GRAMMAR] Verify that a secure forgotten password reset process is implemented that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms._"

The references contain a link to the forgot password cheatsheet.

Thoughts @jmanico @elarlang @ryarmst @randomstuff @TobiasAhnoff ?

comments.body:
I like it Josh. Small change suggestion:

_"[GRAMMAR] Ensure that the secure password reset process enforces the use of multi-factor authentication if it is enabled."_

In case this requirement is with the same level as requirement for MFA, we can remove conditional MFA part. Current requirement is Level 2:
> V2.2.9 Verify that the application requires users to either use a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a requires a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms.	

Requirement starts with "Verify that".

One shortened version:
> Verify that a ~~secure~~ forgotten password reset process ~~is implemented that~~ does not bypass any ~~enabled~~ multi-factor authentication mechanisms.

> "[GRAMMAR] Ensure that the secure password reset process enforces the use of multi-factor authentication if it is enabled."

> Verify that a ~~secure~~ forgotten password reset process ~~is implemented that~~ does not bypass any ~~enabled~~ multi-factor authentication mechanisms.

I'm a bit concerned that both these proposals bury the point that it is important to have a secure forgot password process and that the MFA point is an additional to this.

@tghosth Was the primary intent of 2.5.6 to mitigate account takeover through email hijacking (via subsequent password reset)? I think mandating MFA is probably a necessary component of this. It could be abstracted more, but I think it might then be unclear with respect to what is required to be implemented. 

Are we re-examining 2.5.7?

(Adding MFA is good and all. On the other side, enforcing more MFA everywhere (combined with automatic account lockdown after suspicious activity detection based on some machine learning model) is a very good way to make the probability that the normal people looses access to all his accounts tend to 1 as time goes by. :smile:)

> @tghosth Was the primary intent of 2.5.6 to mitigate account takeover through email hijacking (via subsequent password reset)? I think mandating MFA is probably a necessary component of this. It could be abstracted more, but I think it might then be unclear with respect to what is required to be implemented.

I think the primary intent is to have a secure forgot password process. Email hijacking will certainly be hard to mitigate in a single-factor auth situation. This is why the in addition to the primary intent, my suggestion clarifies that this should not bypass MFA.

> Are we re-examining 2.5.7?

I think 2.5.7 is ok and I brought it in to explain why I think we are already covered on MFA and that we don't want use of MFA to confuse 2.5.6.

> (Adding MFA is good and all. On the other side, enforcing more MFA everywhere (combined with automatic account lockdown after suspicious activity detection based on some machine learning model) is a very good way to make the probability that the normal people looses access to all his accounts tend to 1 as time goes by. 😄)

This is part of the reason that I want 2.5.6 to be simple and clear.

@elarlang @jmanico @ryarmst @randomstuff any further comments on what I wrote above, as a reminder, I still propose:

"_[MODIFIED] Verify that a secure forgotten password reset process is implemented that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms._"

How about a positive take on this:

_[MODIFIED] Verify that a secure forgotten password reset process is implemented so that it includes a multi-factor authentication mechanism._

> [MODIFIED] Verify that a secure forgotten password reset process is implemented so that it includes a multi-factor authentication mechanism.

I don't think that we can mandate that a forgot password actively includes MFA, I would rather keep the topics separate. This is intended to be a simple requirement which basically says follow the cheatsheet and don't bypass MFA if it is enabled. Elsewhere we will talk about the importance of MFA. I am going to open a PR.

> forgotten password reset process

It can be read as "a process about password reset that is forgotten".
"_[MODIFIED] Verify that a secure process for resetting a forgotten password is implemented, that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms._"

We can add brackets a well.
> Verify that a secure process for resetting a (forgotten) password is implemented, that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms.

With or without brackets, please update the PR.

title: Forgot password requirement 2.5.6 is confusing
